searchStringsArray.title: 🔍 Search terms
searchStringsArray.description: What to search for on Google Maps, e.g. restaurant or dentist. Each term runs as a separate search, combined with the 📍 Location below. You can also include a location directly in the term (e.g. dentist Austin TX).

locationQuery.title: 📍 Location
locationQuery.description: Location appended to every search term, e.g. New York, USA or Berlin, Germany. Leave empty if your search terms or start URLs already define a location.

maxCrawledPlacesPerSearch.title: Number of places per search term
maxCrawledPlacesPerSearch.description: Maximum number of places collected per search term (before filtering). Google Maps itself rarely returns more than ~120 results per search — split a big city into neighborhoods or ZIP codes for more coverage.

maxCrawledPlaces.title: Total number of places (all searches)
maxCrawledPlaces.description: Overall cap on saved places across all search terms and start URLs. Leave empty for no cap. The run stops once this many places have been saved.

language.title: Language
language.description: Results are localized to this language (Google's hl parameter).

categoryFilterWords.title: 🎢 Place categories
categoryFilterWords.description: Only include places whose category matches one of these words, e.g. restaurant, hotel. Matching is case-insensitive and matches partial category names (restaurant also matches Sushi restaurant). Leave empty to keep all categories.
categoryFilterWords.sectionDescription: Narrow down which places are saved to the dataset. All filters combine — a place must pass every one.

searchMatching.title: Match search terms in place names
searchMatching.description: Restrict results to places whose name matches the search term. Useful for finding all locations of a specific brand.
enumTitles: Place name must include the search term
Place name must exactly match the search term

placeMinimumStars.title: ⭐ Minimum star rating
placeMinimumStars.description: Only include places rated at least this many stars. Places with no rating yet are excluded when this is set.

maximumStars.title: Maximum star rating
maximumStars.description: Only include places rated at most this many stars (0–5), e.g. 3.5. Leave empty to disable. Useful for finding poorly rated businesses.

minReviewsCount.title: Minimum number of reviews
minReviewsCount.description: Only include places with at least this many reviews. Set to 0 to disable.

maxReviewsCount.title: Maximum number of reviews
maxReviewsCount.description: Only include places with at most this many reviews. Leave empty to disable. Useful for finding smaller businesses.

website.title: 🌐 Websites filter
website.description: Filter places by whether they list a website. Only without a website is handy for web-design/marketing lead generation.

phone.title: 📞 Phone numbers filter
phone.description: Filter places by whether they list a contact phone number. Only without a phone number can help find businesses with incomplete listings.
enumTitles: Only places with a phone number
Only places without a phone number

skipClosedPlaces.title: ⛔ Skip closed places
skipClosedPlaces.description: Skip places marked as temporarily or permanently closed.

startUrls.title: Start URLs
startUrls.description: Google Maps URLs to scrape directly — either search URLs (google.com/maps/search/...) or place URLs (google.com/maps/place/...). Runs in addition to the search terms above.
startUrls.sectionDescription: Direct URLs, output tweaks, and proxy settings.

exportPlaceUrls.title: Export only place URLs from search
exportPlaceUrls.description: Save name, rating, review count, and place URL straight from the search results without opening each place page. Much faster and cheaper, but the dataset won't contain phone, website, address, or category — and filters that need those fields (websites filter, categories, closed places) are not applied.

proxyConfiguration.title: Proxy configuration
proxyConfiguration.description: Proxy to use for scraping. Apify residential proxies are strongly recommended — Google blocks datacenter IPs quickly.
